# Quantum Phase Drift Capacity

The project studies the quantum communication redundancy and diagnostic cost of phase noise on a qubit train. A pair of smooth, stationary phase processes can have parametrically different capacity deficits even when their complete channels agree on every selection of up to 2r+1 carriers. For the separate Brownian drift and uniform-reset comparison, the complete channels agree through three slots and the binary discrimination cost at fixed error depends sharply on input entanglement depth.

## Choose a reading route

- Story: README.md states the question and results; science/README.md connects the mechanisms and physical interpretation.
- Study: learning/README.md introduces the one selected anchor, John Preskill's Quantum Information Chapter 10, Quantum Shannon Theory, updated June 2025. learning/anchor-and-bridge.md maps source sections and notation to the project. learning/milestones.md is the shared map of exactly 30 targets: 12 background/preliminaries and 18 narrative/innovation milestones, with dependencies and sources.
- Theorems and proofs: science/model-and-blocking.md fixes the channel, resources and operational capacity and proves exact product blocking. science/brownian-capacity.md gives the achievable entropy bound, arbitrary-encoder converse and coefficient limitations. science/reset-capacity.md gives coherent-environment pinching, finite-code Schmidt-rank bounds and renewal limits. science/indistinguishability.md proves equality through three selected slots, the four-slot diagnostic and the redundancy ratio. science/discrimination-and-depth.md establishes exact four-slot optimality and the optimal consecutive-carrier order max{kappa^(-1/3), (kappa*d)^(-1/2)} at depth d, with matching probes and converses.
- Growing diagnostic windows: science/growing-diagnostics.md constructs smooth phase laws by splitting a periodic second-derivative stencil into jump generators and adding Brownian components. It proves equality through 2r+1 selected carriers at arbitrary gaps, gives the first witness at 2r+2, and separates the optimal capacity deficits at fixed cadence. Its absolute capacity interval has width log2(n+1)/n and uses the optimized coherent information of the n-carrier block.
- Reproduction: verification/README.md documents the finite diagnostics, parameters and limits; verification/check_phase_drift.py is the runnable source and verification/expected-results.json records the reference output.
- Attribution: references/related-work.md compares the closest precedents and imported ingredients; references/references.bib contains structured bibliographic entries. Primary research references supplement the single educational anchor.

Use the authoritative topic pages for exact claims. The learning bridge explains their connections without replacing the full proofs.

- Timestamped distillation: science/timestamped-entanglement.md specializes the smooth match to r=1 and identifies the link-state correspondence, the four-herald test, and the clean Poisson distillation-rate separation.

## Preserve the scientific distinctions

Every physical carrier counts, including pilots and padding. Capacity takes the train-length limit at fixed cadence and fixed noise before the small-noise limit. The phase trajectory is hidden. A passive reference is allowed for the selected-carrier channel comparisons. The fixed-error discrimination law concerns the specified Brownian and uniform-reset pair with known matched parameters. Depth constrains preparation groups and their private references, and joint receiver measurements are allowed. The growing-window witness gives a first distinct subchannel and does not establish the repetition cost of distinguishing the new pair. The absolute capacity interval uses a finite optimization whose efficiency is unspecified. Exact leading capacity coefficients and the optimal carrier threshold for relative redundancy estimation remain open.
